title: The Last Light
lesson: Paper says who. People only say what they saw.
intro: On the night of the Harvest Ball, in a rising gale, the lamp at Wren Point went dark. The trawler Merry Wren ran onto the Mallow Rocks. Her skipper rowed ashore, but the boat was lost.

The coastguard logged the light burning at 22:05. At 22:36 the Grand's doorman telephoned to say it was out. Someone climbed the tower and jammed the lamp's clockwork with a marlinspike, which takes at least six minutes.
The keeper, his daughter, a fisherman with a grudge and the boat's owner all have stories. One of them is wearing someone else's coat.

people.name: Nell Garrow
people.blurb: The keeper's daughter, seventeen. Was meant to be minding the lamp tonight.

people.name: Elias Garrow
people.blurb: Keeper of Wren Point for twenty-two years. Night off. Darts.

people.name: Bertram Cole
people.blurb: Fisherman, doorman at the Grand on Saturdays. Swore he'd see Rook ruined.

people.name: Capt. Augustus Rook
people.blurb: Owner of the Merry Wren. At the Harvest Ball all night, or so the photographs say.

clocks.name: The Lantern's bar clock
clocks.note: Ten minutes slow. We learned that at the Regatta.

clocks.name: Press camera date-back
clocks.note: Wendell Fry never sets his camera's clock.

incident.title: The Last Light
incident.text: Wren Point's lamp clockwork was jammed with a marlinspike. Burning at 22:05 (coastguard), reported dark at 22:36. The job takes 6 minutes at the top of the tower.

cards.title: Fault log
cards.text:
Supply dip, Wrenhaven East feeder.
Duration: 3 seconds. Cause: gale on the lines.

cards.title: Roll 3, frame 11
cards.text:
The ballroom mid-waltz as every chandelier dips at once.
Date-back stamp: 22:10

cards.title: Nell Garrow
cards.text: “I was up in the lamp room all night, from nine till Dad came running in. I never left the light. Not once.”
cards.reply: “…I went to the pictures with Davey. Dad says boys are a distraction from the light. I'm sorry. I'm so sorry.”

cards.title: Box office ledger
cards.text:
21:30 · BACK TO THE FUTURE
2 × stalls · N. GARROW

cards.title: Davey Penhale
cards.text: “Nell and me were in the back row of the Odeon from half nine till the end, five past eleven. She never left my side.”
cards.firm: “Never left my side. I swear it on my mum.”

cards.title: Sid Barrow
cards.text: “Elias was at the oche from nine by our clock till about quarter past ten, when young Jory burst in shouting that the Point was dark.”
cards.firm: “Nine till quarter past ten by the clock. Yes, that clock. I know, I know.”

cards.title: Darts slate
cards.text:
E. GARROW · checked out on double sixteen
Time chalked off the clock over the bar.

cards.title: Coastguard log
cards.text:
E. Garrow telephones from Wren Point:
lamp clockwork jammed with a marlinspike. Restarting.

cards.title: Mrs Pengelly
cards.text: “I saw Bertram Cole in his yellow oilskin, the one with the patched elbow, hurrying along the cliff path towards the Point. St Brigid's had just struck the quarter.”
cards.reply: “Well… it was his oilskin. Nobody else has a patch like that. I never saw his face, not with the hood up in that rain.”

cards.title: Exchange log
cards.text:
Grand Hotel front desk → Wrenhaven Taxis · 1 minute
Caller: “Cole, on the door.”

cards.title: Coastguard log
cards.text:
Telephone from the Grand Hotel's doorman, B. Cole:
“Wren Point's gone dark.”

cards.title: Bertram Cole
cards.text: “My oilskin hung on the staff peg by the kitchen door all night. When I fetched it at eleven it was soaked through, with mud to the knees.”
cards.firm: “Soaked. And I never set foot outside all night.”

cards.title: Roll 3, frame 19
cards.text:
The Grand's terrace in the rain. In the background, on the cliff path, a figure in a yellow oilskin heads east.
Date-back stamp: 22:27

cards.title: Capt. Augustus Rook
cards.text: “I was in the ballroom from nine until the band packed up. I danced, I drank, I drew the raffle. I never left it. Ask anyone.”
cards.reply: “Very well. I stepped out onto the terrace for a cigar. Ten minutes. Twenty, perhaps. A man may take the air.”

cards.title: Lavinia Rook
cards.text: “Augustus was at my side the entire evening. We danced every dance.”
cards.reply: “I… danced two reels with the Mayor. When I came back, Augustus was at the bar and his hair was wet. He said he'd been on the terrace. I chose to believe him.”

cards.title: Roll 3, frame 14
cards.text:
Capt. Rook toasts the Mayor beneath the big chandelier.
Date-back stamp: 22:12

cards.title: Roll 3, frame 22
cards.text:
Capt. Rook draws the raffle, beaming, hair oddly damp.
Date-back stamp: 22:56

triggers.question: Nell says she never left the lamp room, but the Odeon sold her two stalls tickets at 21:25.
Mrs Pengelly saw Cole on the cliff path at 22:15. The exchange has him ringing for a taxi from the hotel desk at 22:14, four minutes' walk away.
The figure in the oilskin can only be Rook, and Rook says he never left the ballroom.

triggers.memo: Fry's camera runs twelve minutes fast. Every photograph on that roll just moved.
Only one face is left. The oilskin had a passenger.

memos.text: Some cards don't say who. Watch the faces: paper can rule a person out, words can't.
A face is crossed out when that person's paper trail makes the card impossible. When only one is left, you've found them.
Every alibi holds. Then look at whose clock they hang on.

reconstruction: 22:08. Rook slips out of the ballroom, past the kitchens, and lifts Cole's oilskin off its peg.
22:15. Fry's flash catches a yellow shape on the cliff path. Nobody looks twice.
22:23. A marlinspike in the lamp's clockwork. Wren Point goes dark.
22:41. Back in the ballroom with wet hair. “Just a cigar on the terrace.”
22:44. He draws the raffle and smiles for the camera.
epilogue: Rook had insured the Merry Wren for twice her worth in September. His nephew Tam was to run her onto the Mallow Rocks at low water and row ashore: “the light failed, nobody's fault.”
The insurers paid nothing. Tam turned King's evidence. Mrs Pengelly sent Cole a fruit cake by way of apology.
Nell still minds the light. Davey brings the choc-ices. Connie's note: “Three for three, partner. Go home and get some sleep.”
